PC: 1. Suction airway 2. Calculate fluids 3. Set up and administer fluids using equipment in crash cart
First Person: Enters the room, checks for responsiveness, sees difficulty breathing, cyanosis, and hypoxia.

Expected Actions:
Second responder enters and gets gloves as the First Person conducts rapid assessment of perfusion, respiratory examination including airway, breath sounds, and pulse oximeter reading.
Both responders should help get oxygen applied to the patient, ideally nasal cannula, and then prepare to suction with a catheter.
Administer bolus 20mL/kg of Normal Saline (NS) or Lactated Ringers (LR) via push-pull method.
SBP: “Patient is in distress. I need help!” pushes code button and then gets gloves.
ICS: “She has a pulse, has secretions in her airway, and is breathing adequately.”
After suctioning and oxygen, team leader should share partial mental model recognizing tachycardia and compensated shock.
Team Leader: Share Mental Model (three problems: hypoxia, airway clearance, compensated shock now improving)
